name: Atlanta
summary: The capital of the New South — the world's busiest airport city, home of Coca-Cola and CNN, a world-class aquarium, and the cradle of the civil-rights movement. The region's climax before the trip turns to Florida.

lodging.name: A Midtown or Downtown Atlanta hotel
lodging.blurb: Midtown for the museums and the BeltLine; Downtown for the aquarium and parks.

foodMustTry.name: Fried chicken & a Varsity chili dog
foodMustTry.blurb: Southern soul food, and a chili dog at the world's largest drive-in.

days.label: Day 200 — Downtown icons
days.summary: The capitol, Coke, and an aquarium.

item.title: Georgia State Capitol
item.blurb: The gold-domed capitol (the gold is real, from Dahlonega) in the heart of downtown.

item.title: Georgia Aquarium & World of Coca-Cola
item.blurb: One of the largest aquariums on earth (whale sharks!), next to the World of Coca-Cola and Centennial Olympic Park.

item.title: Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park

location.name: Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park

item.blurb: Dr. King's birth home, Ebenezer Baptist Church, and the King Center where he and Coretta are entombed.

item.title: National Center for Civil and Human Rights

location.name: National Center for Civil and Human Rights
location.address: 100 Ivan Allen Jr Blvd NW, Atlanta, GA

item.blurb: Immersive galleries linking the American movement to global human rights.

days.label: Day 202 — Art & the BeltLine
days.summary: High culture and Atlanta's great urban trail.

item.title: The High Museum of Art
item.blurb: The Southeast's leading art museum, in a landmark Richard Meier building.

item.title: The Atlanta BeltLine & Ponce City Market

location.name: Ponce City Market
location.address: 675 Ponce De Leon Ave NE, Atlanta, GA

item.blurb: A rails-to-trails loop of murals and breweries, anchored by the food hall at Ponce City Market.

days.label: Day 203 — Free Day
days.summary: A theme park, a monolith, or a ballgame. Options below.

freeMenu.title: Stone Mountain Park

location.name: Stone Mountain Park
location.address: 1000 Robert E Lee Blvd, Stone Mountain, GA

freeMenu.blurb: The largest exposed granite monolith in the world — a cable car, trails, and a laser show.

freeMenu.title: Six Flags Over Georgia
freeMenu.blurb: A big regional coaster park west of the city.

freeMenu.title: A Braves game at Truist Park
freeMenu.blurb: Baseball in season at The Battery entertainment district.

days.label: Day 204 — South to Florida
days.summary: Leave Georgia for the Sunshine State — the Coastal Southeast is done.

commute.scenicNote: A long southward run into Florida and warmer winter days.
